# The twelve findings, what each one takes, and what not to touch

The first review that read this diff returned it. Four triages before it never got a
model to the code, which is the thing to read the twelve findings against: they are
the first reading of the work itself, and the rule set they read holds. All 22
registry entries cross-check both ways, every fixture is a genuine violation of its
own rule rather than a file its tool happens to dislike, the three fixtures
criterion 2 names by hand are all present, and the reviewer checked by hand that the
dependency-cruiser rule replacing the deleted `packages/providers/src/boundary.ts`
is at parity or better. None of that needs revisiting.

What it returns on is the account, and the loop around the rules.

## The three in the ticket file, which are the ones that cannot wait

F2, F3 and F5 are in the Outcome and the amendment, and the ticket file is covered
by the reviewed-tree fingerprint, so they cannot be corrected after a review passes
without another return. Do them first.

- **F2.** Three figures disagree with the records the accepted tdd record cites.
  1,521 tests is attempts 3 to 5; the regression this record cites is 168 at 1,548.
  The hook figure 0.66s over 51 paths is record 31 from attempt 2; the budget
  evidence now cited is record 157, 937ms over 55 paths, 34 files through Biome and
  46 modules through dependency-cruiser. 1.45s for the tree run is in no record at
  all: the only tree run is 135 at 1.324s. Correct all three, and name the record
  each figure comes from, which is what F2's rule candidate asks for.
- **F3.** The Outcome counts its own returns ("two returns to solution against a
  target of 0.5") and its own sessions ("four sessions, one orchestrating and
  three implementers"). ADR-0004 forbids both outright, and this review is the
  proof of why: there are seven return records now, and `kpi.rework` counts every
  one. Delete the counts rather than correcting them. The KPI report is where a
  reader gets that number, from the journal, which cannot be wrong.
- **F5.** Criterion 1's amendment defers eleven modules of `packages/core/db/` to
  "a ticket of its own, named in the Outcome", and the Outcome says only "Its own
  ticket". There is no id and no file. Either write the ticket and name it, which
  is the honest reading of the amendment, or rewrite the amendment to say the work
  is unticketed. Those eleven modules are SEEN-008's trade-record schema and its
  tests, and nothing compiles them today.

## F4, the one that is about the rule set itself

The registry names no entry for the two tools with no configuration file, so the
ground rule about a live marketplace host in a test has no rule id. `harness/rules.py`
says in as many words that gitleaks and the harness's own checks are in the set
because they run in the same hook, and record 38 settled that the registry carries
the harness check as the rule with no duplicate written. Neither entry exists. A
reviewer giving a finding `harness/no-live-marketplace-host` as its candidate gets
it counted as recurring with no rule, which is the loop reporting a rule missing
because its own map omits it. Two entries, each with a citation and a fixture, and
`rules --check` already holds a tool with no configuration to both.

## F1 and F6, untested wiring

Both are a line between a function and its caller, with the function tested and the
line not. F1: nothing runs `harness report --week` and asserts the three lists are
in it, so `cli.py`'s weekly branch and the eighth argument to `reporting.render`
could both go with the suite green. F6: `rule_candidate` is asserted on the review
advance by eight cases and on `harness return --findings` by none, and that is the
path the Outcome singles out as the one that matters. Both are a test each, in files
the slice plan already names.

## F7, the graph

`graphify-out/` is not updated for a branch that adds the whole rule set, and every
comparable merged harness ticket carried its update. Worth reading the reviewer's
last sentence on it: the post-commit hook CLAUDE.md describes is not in this
repository, `.githooks` holds only `pre-commit`, so nothing was going to do this by
itself. Run `graphify update .` and commit the result, and consider whether the
missing hook is a finding against the harness rather than against this ticket.

## The five low findings

F8 to F12 are an evidence gap (no recorded `pnpm turbo run test` or `build`,
although CI runs both), a citation checked to the file and not to the section, two
HTTP libraries missing from one deny-list, a sentence in `workflow.md` that still
says knip runs in the hook, and a clarify evidence line about
`harness/templates/review.json` that was never answered. F11 is one sentence and
should be done with the medium findings. The other four are a judgement about
whether they are this ticket's or a follow-up's; whichever way they go, say so.

## What this round is, for the tdd record

A round of rework belonging to no single slice: declare `null` for its position and
run it on opus at high effort, which is slice 1's route and the strictest in the
plan. Every pair in the accepted record, 158 to 167, was recorded against a tree
that any of these fixes moves, so the replay recipe is the one in record 109 and in
`.harness-drafts/replay2.sh`: revert each slice's own production files, record the
red, restore, record the green, then the regression and the coverage last, in that
order.
